submission.justification: Sensor-T3 gives the best unirradiated resolution (6.0 um at 150 um in the 2025 summary). But after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency drops to 82.0%, well below the 97% end-of-life requirement for the innermost layer, so it is ruled out. Of the two radiation-suitable options, T1 (98.5%) has much better resolution than T2 (99.2%), which gives 14.3-19.0 um. A thickness scan of T1 gave 10.65 um at 50 um, 9.78 at 100, 9.24 at 125, 8.39 and 8.71 at 150 (two runs), 9.35 at 175, 9.40 at 200 and 12.37 at 300, so the optimum is around 150 um. The two repeat runs at 150 um differ by about 0.3 um, which shows statistical spread between runs. Caveats: the simulated resolutions are for unirradiated sensors only. Resolution after irradiation was not simulated or measured. The test-beam efficiency figures do not state a sensor thickness, so it is assumed that 150 um T1 keeps its >=97% efficiency.

requirements.evidence: Of the radiation-suitable options, T1 at 150 um gave the best simulated result: 8.4-8.7 um unirradiated, against >=14.3 um for T2. T3 resolves better (6.0 um) but is excluded on radiation grounds. Resolution after irradiation is not known.

requirements.requirement: Sensor is one of the three technologies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T1 (planar, standard pitch) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for the innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% efficiency to end of life)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md: T1 has 98.5% hit efficiency after 2e16 neq/cm^2, above the 97% requirement (T3 has 82.0%). The test thickness is not stated.
150 um is within the allowed range.
